author: A Robot
objectives: Identify and name the four heart chambers, the four major valves, and the principal vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Trace the path of blood through the heart in dual-loop circulation (pulmonary and systemic) in correct sequence.
Differentiate pulmonary vs systemic circuits based on oxygenation status and vessel directionality.
Explain the left vs right ventricular myocardium thickness asymmetry using pressure/resistance requirements.
Describe valve function (atrioventricular vs semilunar) and how valves prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.

modules.description: Introduce two patient-oriented heart models (exterior and cutaway) and guide gross anatomical orientation and mirroring.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Recognize the heart’s apex orientation (downward and slightly to the left from an anatomical view).
Determine patient right vs patient left when viewed from the learner’s perspective.
Locate major entering/leaving vessels on the exterior model for later tracing.
instructions: Rotate your device to inspect labels from different angles.
Use the apex marker to keep track of anatomical orientation while you trace structures later.

components.text: Orientation reminder: anatomical right/left is patient-based, so your view is mirrored.

clips.changeMeaning: Spawns both heart models with an orientation label and an apex marker to ground anatomical perspective.
clips.narration: Welcome! This lab uses two views: an exterior heart model and a cutaway heart model with chambers and valves exposed. Remember: anatomical descriptions use the patient’s orientation, so your view is mirrored.

clips.changeMeaning: Both heart models rotate to a clearer angle for seeing landmarks and internal relationships.
clips.narration: Rotate the models together. Notice which side appears to contain the patient’s right atrium and right ventricle.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlights key exterior vessels (SVC, IVC, pulmonary trunk, aorta) while keeping the apex marker aligned.
clips.narration: On the intact heart, locate vessels entering and leaving: superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary trunk, and the aorta. These will anchor the blood-path tracing later.

modules.moduleName: Scene 2 — Guided Structural Tour (Chambers, Valves, Vessels)
modules.description: Sequentially highlight chambers, then valves, then major vessels on the cutaway while mirroring the corresponding exterior landmarks.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Name the four chambers in order: RA → RV → LA → LV.
Name valves and their chamber relationships: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, aortic.
Recall the major vessels entering/leaving in order for later tracing: SVC, IVC, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta.
Explain the mitral/bicuspid naming as used in anatomy and clinical contexts.
instructions: Watch the highlight order and match each cutaway structure to the similar exterior region.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlights the right atrium on the cutaway and mirrors the region on the exterior map, updating the on-screen label.
clips.narration: First, the four chambers. We start with the right atrium: the entry chamber receiving blood returning from the body.

clips.changeMeaning: Moves highlighting to the right ventricle and updates label text to continue RA → RV.
clips.narration: Next is the right ventricle, which pumps blood onward toward the lungs.

clips.changeMeaning: Transitions to the left atrium on both models and updates the label to LA.
clips.narration: Now the left atrium receives oxygenated blood coming back from the lungs.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlights the tricuspid valve between RA and RV and updates the label to anchor valve-chamber relationships.
clips.narration: Valves maintain one-way flow. The tricuspid valve sits between the right atrium and right ventricle.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlights the pulmonary valve and updates label text to continue valve sequence.
clips.narration: The pulmonary valve controls outflow from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlights the mitral (bicuspid) valve and explicitly shows the dual naming on the label.
clips.narration: This valve is called the mitral valve or the bicuspid valve—same structure between the left atrium and left ventricle.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlights the aortic valve between the left ventricle and aorta, completing the valve inventory in sequence.
clips.narration: The aortic valve controls outflow from the left ventricle into the aorta.
